lockedStoryRule: The mystery is WHAT is bleeding through from the forgotten war and WHAT HAPPENS if it fully returns. The story is not about HOW the phenomenon works.
governingPremise: The forgotten civilization is not advanced technology awaiting explanation. Its history was so enormous that reality itself remembers it. Places, matter, bodies, dreams, loyalties and institutions can remember what conscious history erased.

warriorGodArchitecture.storyFunction: The warrior gods/champions are a second dramatic cast. The forgotten war is exposed through remembered or visionary vignettes in which the ancient characters interact with one another as full people, not as explanatory manifestations.
warriorGodArchitecture.revealRule: Introduce one previously unseen warrior god/champion per issue. Previously introduced ancient characters may recur. Do not front-load multiple new pantheon members into the same issue.
warriorGodArchitecture.witnessRule: Theo and Rae initially experience these scenes as memory-bearers and witnesses. They should not casually converse with ancient figures, receive tutorials from them, or treat them as interactive holograms. Direct modern/ancient interaction, if it ever occurs, must be a later earned development.
warriorGodArchitecture.theoAncientRole: Junior attaché to General Mero; present at strategy sessions and negotiations, never a champion or front-line fighter.
warriorGodArchitecture.raeAncientRole: Strategic aide to Arbiter; recorded rulings, enforcement decisions and civilization-scale consequences.
warriorGodArchitecture.adrianAncientRole: Neutral envoy, courier and facilitator between factions; created routes and safe corridors, witnessed both sides, and initiated the Reset with General Mero's authorization.
warriorGodArchitecture.expositionRule: Historical exposition should emerge from conflict, affection, rivalry, judgment, grief, loyalty and betrayal among the ancient cast. Do not turn memory scenes into lore lectures.

revisionRules: Aggressively remove fake precision: measurements, temperatures, frequencies, percentages, angles, exact distances, thresholds, tolerances, diagnostic readouts and pseudo-scientific causal explanation unless an ordinary practical detail is indispensable to the immediate action.
No character speaks in engineering-tolerance language. Theo, Rae, Adrian, Vark and institutional figures use distinct human voices.
Characters may observe, recognize, compare, remember, fear and form theories. They do not solve the phenomenon as a mechanism.
Every discovery should deepen WHAT this is, WHAT happened before, WHY someone remembers it, WHAT is returning, or WHAT the consequence of return will be.
If removing a technical explanation makes a moment stranger, more frightening or more emotionally meaningful, remove it.
Preserve meaningful physical acting but remove quantified choreography and prose that explains motivations already visible in behavior.
Break the repeated scene template of technical argument plus hand-blocking plus physiological diagnosis.
Add ordinary human-scale behavior, humor, irritation, fatigue, affection and silence so cosmic events have contrast.
Ration signature spectacle. Violet light, impossible geometry and celestial imagery are motifs, not constant wallpaper.
Protect the causal spine and locked arc unless a genuine continuity failure is discovered.
Memory is admissible dramatic evidence. Recognition can be more important than measurement.
Mystery survives discovery: answers reveal history and consequence, not operating instructions.
Treat each warrior god/champion as a complete dramatic character with relationships, contradictions, loyalties, grievances, culpability and an evolving historical arc.
A memory vignette must work as a scene even if Theo and Rae are removed from its dialogue. The ancient characters should want things from one another in the moment.
Do not use a warrior god merely to explain an artifact, power, mechanism or rule of the universe.

characterVoiceTargets.Theo: Obsessive, intuitive, frightened by recognition and increasingly compelled by memory. He sounds like a person trying to prove an impossible memory is real, not a cartographer explaining instrumentation.
characterVoiceTargets.Rae: Incisive, skeptical, observant and self-controlled. She notices patterns and institutional suppression but does not convert terror into diagnostics.
characterVoiceTargets.Adrian: Restrained, burdened and evasively knowledgeable. He often knows what something means but refuses to say why. His authority comes from history and consequence, not clinical precision.
characterVoiceTargets.Vark: Practical, experienced, dry and grounded. His contrast comes from ordinary work, common sense and concern for people, not compliance jargon.
characterVoiceTargets.Caelum: Institutional, political and controlling. He is concerned with order, exposure and consequence, not technical trivia.

continuityQuestion: At every scene boundary ask: what new thing has the audience learned about WHAT is returning, WHO these ancient people were, or WHAT it could cost? If the answer is only HOW an anomaly behaves, rewrite the scene.
